columnPool.label: Route: Castle Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Castle Line route
columnPool.hint: The route north from Nottingham to Lincoln via Newark Castle station - named after the castle stop, not a scenic castle-hopping journey.

columnPool.label: Route: Poacher Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Poacher Line route
columnPool.hint: The 78-mile route from Nottingham through the market towns of Grantham, Sleaford and Boston to the seaside resort of Skegness.

columnPool.label: Route: Humber Linc Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Humber Linc Line route
columnPool.hint: The rural branch from Barton-upon-Humber, near the Humber Bridge, south-east through Grimsby to the seaside resort of Cleethorpes.

columnPool.label: Route: Robin Hood Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Robin Hood Line route
columnPool.hint: The reopened line from Nottingham through Hucknall and Mansfield to Worksop, named for its Sherwood Forest surroundings - closed by Beeching, then reopened in stages through the 1990s.

columnPool.label: Route: Derwent Valley Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Derwent Valley Line route
columnPool.hint: The scenic route from Derby up the Derwent Valley through Belper, Ambergate and Cromford to Matlock, through the Derwent Valley Mills World Heritage Site.

columnPool.label: Route: Erewash Valley
columnPool.display: Is part of the Erewash Valley route
columnPool.hint: The historic freight and passenger route north from Nottingham through the Erewash Valley coalfield towns of Langley Mill, Alfreton and on to Chesterfield.

columnPool.label: Route: Ivanhoe Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Ivanhoe Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Leicester via Loughborough to Nottingham and on to Lincoln - named after Sir Walter Scott's novel, set partly in this area of Leicestershire.

columnPool.label: Route: Birmingham to Leicester Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Birmingham to Leicester Line route
columnPool.hint: The western half of the historic Birmingham-Peterborough cross-country route, linking Birmingham New Street to Leicester via Nuneaton - the only direct rail link between the West Midlands and East Anglia since the Beeching cuts.

columnPool.label: Route: Cathedrals Route
columnPool.display: Is part of the Cathedrals Route route
columnPool.hint: The route from Nottingham via Bottesford and the Vale of Belvoir to the cathedral city of Lincoln, joining the Peterborough-Lincoln line at Spalding.

columnPool.label: Route: Leicester to Peterborough Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Leicester to Peterborough Line route
columnPool.hint: The eastern half of the historic Birmingham-Peterborough cross-country route, linking Leicester to Peterborough via Oakham and Stamford.
